correctness.rationale: Read the full proof and checking source. For invertible binary structure matrix, squares form a basis, so any algebra automorphism has monomial natural-basis columns; over F2 all nonzero scalars are 1, hence automorphism order equals binary directed graph permutation automorphisms. Simplicity corresponds to invertibility and strong connectivity. For even n, I+J is invertible over F2 and S_n-invariant. For odd n>=3, S_n invariance forces a diagonal/off-diagonal two-orbit matrix, which is singular whenever strongly connected. For odd n>=5, a subgroup H with order>(n-1)! would have index<n in S_n; its coset action has nontrivial normal kernel, necessarily A_n, whose 2-transitivity forces the prohibited two-orbit matrix. The hub-and-leaves B_n has determinant 1 in F2 for odd n and stabilizer S_{n-1}; n=3 attains 3 using a directed triangle and n=1 trivial. Independently recalculated binary ranks for full-symmetric even n<=8 and hub odd n<=9; source exhaustive enumeration only n<=4 and is not an all-n proof.
